summary: Add a top-level build.sh launcher that prepares AppForge-LLM v4 from source and opens the existing local web app UI as the primary pipeline entry point.
problem: The app already has a browser-based pipeline, but source users still need to remember several CLI-oriented setup and launch commands before they reach the UI. The requested change is a simpler path where running build.sh brings up the local web app environment directly.
target_users: Local AppForge-LLM v4 users who want to run product-generation pipelines through the browser UI
Developers validating the repository from source without memorizing setup commands
Operators who need a reproducible one-command local web server start on macOS/Linux
desired_outcomes: A repository-root build.sh exists, is executable, and starts the existing appforge web server on a loopback host by default.
The launcher prepares the Python environment and packaged frontend assets when needed, while allowing explicit skip flags for repeat runs and CI smoke checks.
Running the launcher in normal mode opens the web UI automatically through the existing appforge web browser-opening behavior.
The launcher has a non-interactive smoke mode that proves the web UI and health endpoint can start without opening a browser.
README and web-app documentation identify build.sh as the easiest source-start path while preserving CLI compatibility.
constraints: Reuse the existing appforge web FastAPI/Vue production entry point; do not create a second web server or parallel UI.
Keep default binding loopback-only and preserve existing AppForge safety defaults.
Do not deploy, publish, or require external provider credentials.
Do not force llm-bridge usage; the launcher should respect APPFORGE_DRIVER and existing provider configuration.
Avoid destructive repository operations and preserve existing source and tracked AppForge artifacts.
assumptions: Python 3.11+, npm, and the existing project dependency metadata are the supported source-development path.
uv is preferred when available for local dependency sync; a Python venv/pip fallback is acceptable.
Bun/llm_bridge startup is optional and should be activated only when the user selects the llm-bridge driver or explicitly asks the launcher to start it.
A smoke mode may suppress browser opening to keep automated verification deterministic.
non_goals: Do not redesign the Vue UI or change the pipeline runner behavior.
Do not add production daemon management, launch agents, Docker packaging, or hosted deployment.
Do not add new third-party dependencies solely for the launcher.
Do not guarantee live external LLM calls without configured credentials.
Do not remove or deprecate the existing appforge CLI commands.
open_questions: Whether the user wants a separate native desktop wrapper is intentionally out of scope; the safe default is a local browser UI launcher.
Which coding-agent or LLM driver should be used remains runtime configuration through APPFORGE_DRIVER and the existing web health readiness.
